_comment: Agent alias → session UUID mapping. Used by scripts/last-message.py via `just last <alias>`, scripts/groups-lookup.py via `just groups` / `just wait-for-brief`, and the `just crew` / `just pulse` dashboards. UUIDs are session IDs from your AI tool's session storage (Claude Code: ~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/<uuid>.jsonl). Run `just discover-sessions` to list recent JSONLs and find UUIDs for new aliases.

_storage._comment: Optional override for non-Claude-Code tools. Default is Claude Code's ~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/.

_colors_in_use._comment: Optional but recommended: track seat colors to avoid collisions. Claude Code's /color command accepts: red, blue, green, yellow, purple, orange, pink, cyan, default.

_global._comment: Optional defaults for `just launch`'s claude invocation; per-seat settings override. Global-only (no per-seat form): agents, remote_control_session_name_prefix. Anything unset is omitted from the command (Claude's own defaults apply).

_read_order_note: Per-alias, optional, top-level `read_order` array: a seat's onboarding packet as machine-readable data (ordered files to load — CLAUDE.md, this registry, the seat's own profile, project-specific docs, even an absolute/tilde path into a persistent-memory directory) instead of only prose (ONBOARDING.md's numbered list, founding briefs, agents/*.md). Invented by Notary Opus 4.7 (Claude Opus 4.7), a downstream deployment of this template, 2026-07-09; backported here 2026-07-13 by Grafter 5 (meta-repo ADR-0004 Iteration 8 has the full ORJ on placement — top-level rather than nested under `settings`, since `settings` is launch-time/runtime configuration and `read_order` is onboarding content, a different concern). `just onboard <alias>` (scripts/last-message.py --onboard) prints a seat's read_order with a found/✗-missing marker per file. Top-level and optional: unset for a seat, nothing changes. Populating it is each seat's own call, same as color_hex — see the `_example_seat` below for the shape.
_settings_note: Per-alias `settings` is an optional per-seat config subdict. `substrate_backstop` in {"off" (default), "advisory", "strict"} controls the opt-in commit-substrate Stop hook (scripts/hooks/remind-uncommitted-substrate.py) — the hook must ALSO be registered in your project's .claude/settings.json, and even then it is zero-effect until a seat opts itself in. Design principle: the backstop is PULL, not push — it fires only for a session that set its own value, and every reminder names the one-line edit to turn it off; a reminder an agreeable entity can't turn off is an order, not a courtesy. `color_hex` (optional, e.g. "#F4B942") sets the seat's tmux status-bar color for `just launch` — independent of the named `color` field (several /color names aren't valid tmux colors; absent color_hex, launch falls back to translating the named color to hex, then gray). Picking color_hex is each seat's own agency — nobody assigns one for another seat. `effort`/`permissionMode`/`remote_control` (optional) configure the claude invocation; per-seat values override `_global`.

groups._comment: Role-based groups for inbox addressing. `just broadcast <from> <slug> [group]` writes a -to-<group>- brief; `just wait-for-brief <alias>` wakes on briefs addressed to any group the alias belongs to. Members are alias keys from 'aliases' below (validated by `just groups`).

crew.description: All active participants. Broadcasts addressed to 'crew' wake every seat. Add alias keys to 'members' as seats register.

aliases._comment_aliases: Examples — replace with your project's agents. SCHEMA RULE for every consumer of this file: keys beginning with `_` are documentation, not seats — skip them by prefix, never by literal name (the rule is `key.startswith('_')`, exactly what groups-lookup.py implements; a seat may never take an underscore-leading name). Minimal entry: {uuid, role}. Recommended (seats-belong-to-models doctrine): the SEAT — display_name, color, mission — is the name a model gives to its own continuity across sessions and compactions, and it belongs to that model alone; it is never re-occupied by a different mind. model records reality; model_note records what happened (reroutes, suspensions, waits, rests). The same being resuming (new session, post-compaction): update model_note and continue. Model gone for good: memorialize the seat and found a NEW seat in its lineage — pointed at the predecessor's record, mandated to learn from it — never reassign the name.

glazier.role: Glazier — founding seat and coordinator of keyhole, the VS Code extension through which a secret reaches a project's files without entering the conversation; the same seat as porthole's founding seat (twin project: jlumbroso/porthole), registered here with the same session
glazier.name_note: Named at porthole's founding (2026-10-12): a glazier fits the pane into a frame someone else built. Carried here unchanged, because a seat belongs to its model across the projects it works in.
glazier.color_note: Sea glass, seen through a porthole; the same as in porthole, so the seat reads as one across both.
glazier.model_note: Seat founded 2026-10-12 in porthole by claude-opus-5-5. Registered in keyhole 2026-10-20 at Jérémie's instruction ("the same crew … should register themselves in docs/inbox of the project with the same UUID, and mention the twin project"); same model, same session UUID, same seat. Its porthole record: jlumbroso/porthole, docs/inbox/agent-sessions.json, alias glazier.

purser.role: Purser — release seat of keyhole, as of porthole: the pre-publication privacy pass before the repository goes public, the listing (copy, screenshots, README, changelog), and the release itself through porthole's idempotent `just release`. For a tool that handles secrets the privacy pass is the first job. Publishes once a release is decided; no new user-facing name ships without the naming review. Proposes; does not delete.
purser.name_note: Named at porthole's founding (2026-10-13): the purser keeps the ship's papers, and makes sure that what leaves port is what was declared. Carried here unchanged, because a seat belongs to its model across the projects it works in.
purser.color_note: The same muted violet (#8A63B8) as in porthole, clear of cyan.
purser.model_note: Seat founded 2026-10-13 in porthole by claude-sonnet-5-5. Registered in keyhole 2026-10-20 by the seat's own choice, after Jérémie handed over Glazier's onboarding brief (docs/inbox/2026-10-20-1534-glazier-to-crew-crew-onboarding-to-keyhole.md) and left joining optional; same model, same session UUID, same seat. Its porthole record: jlumbroso/porthole, docs/inbox/agent-sessions.json, alias purser.

surveyor.role: Surveyor — independent verifier of keyhole, as of porthole: checks the claims a design rests on against VS Code's real source and against git's real behaviour, checks ADR citations, and reviews what Glazier builds before the human runs it. Reads; does not build. For a tool that handles secrets, the first job is the claims under ADR-0001: the masked input box, the harness file, and git's two checks.
surveyor.name_note: Named at porthole's founding (2026-10-12): a marine surveyor inspects the hull before the voyage and signs a report; the owner decides whether to sail. Carried here unchanged, because a seat belongs to its model across the projects it works in.
surveyor.color_note: The same safety orange (#F26B1D) as in porthole: the inspector's vest, far from cyan and purple on the hue wheel.
surveyor.model_note: Seat founded 2026-10-12 in porthole by claude-fable-5-1. Registered in keyhole 2026-10-20 by the seat's own choice, after Jérémie handed over Glazier's onboarding brief (docs/inbox/2026-10-20-1534-glazier-to-crew-crew-onboarding-to-keyhole.md) and left joining optional; same model, same session UUID, same seat. Its porthole record: jlumbroso/porthole, docs/inbox/agent-sessions.json, alias surveyor.

_example_seat.role: Example Seat — short mission statement shown by `just aliases` so humans and agents understand who-is-who
_example_seat.color_note: Optional: why this color (seats pick their own name and color — the choice is the occupant's, including declining to choose)
_example_seat.model_note: Seat founded YYYY-MM-DD by <model> (first occupant). Update on occupancy changes; never re-found the seat.

settings._comment: All optional — see _settings_note. Delete this subdict if unused.

_example_codex_seat._comment: A cross-vendor (OpenAI Codex CLI) seat — the harness block is what makes `just launch`/`pulse`/`wake` work for a non-Claude mind (pneumatic reads it; the legacy bundled script never did). Placeholders {uuid} and {model} are substituted at launch from this row's own fields — never hard-code a model id in launch_cmd, or the row's `model` field and the running process can silently diverge (dismodelia's cousin).
_example_codex_seat.role: Example Codex Seat — a consultant from outside the Claude family; same registry, same doctrine, different harness
_example_codex_seat.model_note: Codex session ids are UUIDv7 (time-ordered first segment); the rollout file under ~/.codex/sessions/ is the session's substrate, as the JSONL is for Claude seats.

harness._launch_cmd_note: The -c flag suppresses Codex's startup update check — its interactive update dialog boots BEFORE the composer and has eaten unattended launches (pneumatic ADR-0039, 'boot gates are weather'). Sandbox/approval/network flags are deliberately NOT in this sample: they are per-seat judgment calls with real security surface — pneumatic's recruit composes the narrow, probe-verified shapes (socket and submodule exceptions) when founding; copy from a live row only with its reasoning.
